name: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies few-shot prompting of a single language model for four mobile-UI interaction tasks, aiming to support conversational interface use without a separate trained model for each task.

name: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). WebShop is one of several evaluation tasks, alongside question answering, fact verification and ALFWorld.
summary: Introduces ReAct, a method that interleaves reasoning traces and actions for language-model agents; WebShop is one of its interactive decision-making evaluations.

name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces recursive criticism and improvement prompting for language-model agents performing computer tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ with a small number of demonstrations per task.

name: Prompting Is All You Need: Automated Android Bug Replay with Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces AdbGPT, a prompting-based approach that uses LLMs to replay app bugs from written reports, applying few-shot examples and reasoning without model training.

name: Learn-by-interact: A Data-Centric Framework for Self-Adaptive Agents in Realistic Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its evaluations also include coding tasks alongside web and desktop environments.
summary: Learn-by-interact synthesizes agent interaction trajectories from documentation and derives instructions from their histories for training or in-context use across web and desktop tasks.

name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.

name: A Training-Free, Task-Agnostic Framework for Enhancing MLLM Performance on High-Resolution Images
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method is task-agnostic and is also evaluated on 4K and 8K image perception.
summary: Introduces Extract Candidate then Predict (ECP), a training-free two-stage method for high-resolution images, evaluated partly on 4K GUI grounding.

name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.

name: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding via Region Consistency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-RC aggregates multiple grounding predictions into spatial voting grids to choose a consensus region. GUI-RCPO then turns agreement with that region into a reward for test-time policy updates on unlabeled GUI screenshots.

name: How Auxiliary Reasoning Unleashes GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies the gap between latent visual grounding and explicit coordinate output in general vision-language models. Three zero-shot methods add axes, grids, or labeled intersections to GUI screenshots so models can express spatial locations without fine-tuning.

name: D-Artemis: A Deliberative Cognitive Framework for Mobile GUI Multi-Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces D-Artemis, a mobile GUI agent framework that retrieves app-specific tips, checks actions before execution, and reflects on their outcomes without trajectory training.

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

name: Mitigating Coordinate Prediction Bias from Positional Encoding Failures
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Vision-PE Shuffle Guidance (VPSG), a training-free correction for coordinate drift in visual models, evaluated for localization on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.

name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.

name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.

name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient High-Resolution GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GUIPruner compresses high-resolution screenshots and interaction history for GUI navigation through training-free resizing and layout-aware token pruning.

name: ST-Lite: Training-Free KV Cache Compression with Spatio-Trajectory Guidance for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ST-Lite, a training-free KV cache compression scheme for vision-language GUI agents that filters redundant frames and preserves small UI elements in interaction traces.

name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with actual GUI-benchmark evaluation; the abstract does not establish a full computer-use policy.
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.

name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.

name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.

name: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported accuracy change is measured on ScreenSpot-Pro.
summary: BAMI uses coarse-to-fine focus and candidate selection at inference time to address precision and ambiguity errors in GUI grounding.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.

name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.

name: AQuaUI: Visual Token Reduction for GUI Agents with Adaptive Quadtrees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AQuaUI reduces screenshot tokens for GUI agents at inference time with adaptive quadtrees that retain spatial positions and reuse prior tree structure across steps.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.

name: A Task-State Representation for Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces TSR, a training-free wrapper for long-horizon mobile GUI agents that tracks instructions, subgoal progress, and action outcomes separately from screen observations.

name: LocalLSTC: A Long Short-Term Control Architecture for Locally Deployed GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces LocalLSTC, a training-free control architecture that maintains persistent task state and uses it to form short execution commitments. Outcomes feed back into that state for progress checks, recovery, and termination in locally deployed desktop agents.

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.

name: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports evaluation on OSWorld-v2 and Agent's Last Exam.
summary: Introduces RSIAgent, a training-free framework that explores unfamiliar digital interfaces, stores environment-specific action knowledge, and reuses that memory for later tasks.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces ExpActivator, which matches the current GUI state to relevant historical states before supplying past actions as guidance. A separate activation rule decides whether a recurring user intent is warranted by the current time and situation or should be withheld.

name: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The main analysis uses DeepPlanning; WebArena-Lite is a transfer setting.
summary: Studies when to improve an LLM agent's runtime harness or train its weights by classifying failed trajectories; WebArena-Lite supplies a web-task transfer test.

name: Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops
notes: The downstream test uses one screenshot-only agent, nine synthetic apps and 60 cached development items, with TAP-tag or text-answer outputs; this is not demonstrated live-app completion. Two catalogs reword the same 40 edits. Re-proposal effects do not establish internal causal mechanisms or task-success gains. Main serving providers were unpinned; rationale labels came from LLM annotators.
summary: Studies repeated rejected edits while optimizing a screenshot-only GUI agent, contrasting static probes with reached loop states and testing how rejection wording changes subsequent edit proposals.

name: From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one application of a broader visual reporting method.
summary: FSR models visual reporting and gives inference-time procedures for frozen vision-language models, including screen parsing and GUI target selection.

name: MPIDetector: Detecting Multi-modal Prompt Injection via LLM-based Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web-agent injections are one evaluation subset of a broader prompt-injection detector.
summary: MPIDetector uses few-shot prompts to detect text and visual prompt injections, with environmental web-agent injections included in its evaluation.

name: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported speedups cover offline multi-image benchmarks and closed-loop OSWorld runs.
summary: Introduces GUIFlow, an incremental inference framework that reuses visual, language, and action computation across successive GUI-agent steps.

name: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluations use Qwen3-VL models on OSWorld-G, ScreenSpot-Pro, and UI-Vision.
summary: Introduces AdaGround, a training-free GUI grounding method that adjusts screenshot zoom to target size and uses a click verifier to refine or reject predictions.

name: MAPLE: A Multimodal Mobile Agent with Playbook-Learned Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MAPLE, a training-free multi-agent framework that shares step-level experience while navigating mobile GUIs and updates prompts during execution.

name: LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Experiments were not reproduced. LongHorizonUI's components run without fine-tuning, with Gemini 2.5 Pro as the default backbone; Appendix D.6 also reports Gemini 1.5 Flash and Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbones. LongGUIBench tasks need more than 15 steps across games and general apps; the paper states 371 scenarios but gives 207 game scenarios in Section 2.1 and 224 in Appendix D.2, and does not name the benchmark's device platform. Other reported evaluations are ScreenSpot grounding, AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey, plus zero-shot AndroidWorld and OSWorld runs in Appendix D.5. The paper points to kane2kang.github.io/LongHorizonUI for code, which was not reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Training-free GUI agent that indexes screen elements via icon detection and OCR, checks each step with multi-level reflection and recovers by fallback clicks or rollback; introduces LongGUIBench, tasks over 15 steps.

name: Are CAPTCHAs Still Bot-hard? Generalized Visual CAPTCHA Solving with Agentic Vision Language Model
notes: Reviewed against the USENIX Security 2025 proceedings PDF and the authors' project page halligan.pages.dev, which the paper names as its website; experiments were not reproduced. In the benchmark comparison Halligan used GPT-4o and acted through PyAutoGUI on CAPTCHAs replayed from a local Flask server. The paper reports 1,577 of 2,600 benchmark challenges solved (60.7%) and a 70.6% average solve rate on previously unseen CAPTCHAs over a 30-day field study run through human-driven CAPTCHA farms. It names Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.15580923 for its source code and benchmark; that archive was not reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Presents Halligan, a VLM agent that abstracts visual CAPTCHAs into frames, elements and keypoints and solves each as a search problem through generated interaction code, tested on 2,600 challenges of 26 types.

publication.venue: Anais do XIV Symposium on Knowledge Discovery, Mining and Learning (KDMiLe 2026)

name: In-Context Teacher–Student Guidance for Open-Weight Browser Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the publisher PDF and the Crossref deposit for its DOI. Experiments have not been independently reproduced. The method, In-Context Learning Guidance (ICLG), has GPT-5.1 solve tasks offline and appends only its reasoning fields, not its low-level actions, to the student prompt; the teacher is not called while the student runs. Evaluation serves the 130 MiniWoB++ tasks locally, caps each run at 5 minutes and 25 interaction steps, counts a score of at least 0.5 as solved, and reports single runs: seven of ten students improve and three lose one task. Retry and refined-prompt ablations cover three students. The paper names no code release or arXiv version.
summary: Training-free protocol that turns a teacher model's offline reasoning traces into prompt guidance for open-weight browser agents; on MiniWoB++ it lifts solved student-task pairs from 208 to 271 across ten students.
